speaker: Abhinavagupta (devotee's voice, first-person recognition)
question: How does the world appear as His, and how is identity declared?
premises: Disclosure first: all this (etad), become of You (tvanmayam), without remainder (aśeṣam), now (idānīm) appears (bhāti) to me (mama) — by the power of Your grace (tvadanugrahaśaktyā).
Then declaration: You (tvaṃ), Maheśa, always (sadaiva) my self (mamātmā); made of my own self (svātmamayaṃ), all (samastam) is mine (mama) through Him (tena).
Grace is the cause of both disclosure and declaration; merit is not.
Appearance, then ownership — the two-step is the pratyabhijñā structure.
uncertainties: Whether 'svātmamaya' means 'made of my self' or 'self-identical' is unresolved.
Whether 'tena' refers to grace or to Maheśa is unresolved.
